name: IST 407 — Machine Learning

vscode._comment_python_envs: python.useEnvironmentsExtension=false removes genuine waste, kept purely as an efficiency fix. ms-python.python lists ms-python.vscode-python-envs in its extensionPack, so every student gets the Environments extension; measured 2026-08-20 it resolved the SAME interpreter /usr/local/bin/python 242 times in 117 seconds. Setting this false stops that churn (its package.json default is already false; an experiment rollout flips it on). Requires a window reload. NOTE: this setting was once suspected of causing the second-notebook hang -- it did NOT. See _comment_stall.
vscode._comment_stall: The 'second-notebook stall' (a cell spins forever on 'Connecting to kernel') was root-caused 2026-08-21 to ipykernel 7.x deadlocking the VS Code Jupyter extension's kernel-startup handshake on the 2nd/3rd kernel. FIX: ipykernel is pinned <7 in requirements.txt. The kernel is healthy underneath (it answers kernel_info from a plain jupyter_client); only VS Code's registration hangs. Days were lost wrongly blaming Pylance -- disabling Pylance only appeared to fix it because the stall is intermittent (the eslint/autopep8 confound all over again). Pylance, Copilot, DNS, filesystem, and python.analysis.nodeExecutable were ALL falsified by measurement. Do NOT re-add languageServerMode:light or python.analysis.indexing:false as 'stall mitigations' -- they aimed at the wrong target and only degrade IntelliSense on a 126-file repo where full Pylance is fine.

postCreateCommand: git remote add upstream https://github.com/SU-IST407-FS26/ist407-fs26-student.git 2>/dev/null || true; git config --global --add safe.directory "$PWD" 2>/dev/null || true; python -c "import sklearn; print('IST407 environment OK - sklearn', sklearn.__version__)"
